title: SmoothAndConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a globally convex differentiable function f:E→ℝ, with an attained global minimum. Strong convexity is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex.spec.admissible, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f and the existential IsMinOn condition.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x∈E returns ∇f(x), exactly, for every call index and oracle seed. Gradient uniqueness makes the reply independent of those indices and seeds. Function values are not supplied. Execution makes one gradient call per iteration with a fixed budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible.HasGradientAt condition; LongTails/Template.lean: _run, execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary real Hilbert space. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, with L>0. A global minimizer xstar satisfies ‖x0−xstar‖≤R, where R≥0. E, L and x0 are public; R and ε>0 are hidden parameters used to specify the execution budget and success criterion. No dimension bound or bounded feasible domain is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm receives S.Public.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for an attained global minimizer xstar. No distance or gradient-norm accuracy is required.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap inequality holds almost surely under the execution's joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed law. Success is not stated in expectation, and algorithms may be randomized.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.successful, ∀ᵐ ω ∂P; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.law, Oracle.law and Convergence product measure.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard smooth convex minimization benchmark with an exact gradient oracle, known smoothness constant, initial distance bound and objective-gap accuracy, formulated in a real Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Smooth Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, where L>0, and a given starting point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives only E, L, and x0; the radius R and tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. Here the minimizer is fixed independently of the algorithm’s randomness; any global minimizer gives the same objective value.

comparisonHtml:
A convex differentiable f:E→R on a real Hilbert space has an L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0, and a minimizer x⋆ with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, R≥0. The oracle returns the exact gradient for every query and seed. Target: f(xK)−f(x⋆)≤ε, ε>0, almost surely under every oracle seed law. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction; the constructions use known L, with R,ε determining the stopping budget.

Smooth convex minimization: SmoothAndConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) AcceleratedConvex (Ours) (review) O(1+LR2/ε)
(2) GdConvex (Ours) (review) O(1+LR2/ε)
(3) Nesterov AGD (d’Aspremont et al. 2021, Cor. 4.9) O(1+LR2/ε) (1): Matches known rate; Lean formalization. The dimension-free argument extends to Hilbert spaces. (2): For LR2/ε≫1, about LR2/(8ε) times more calls. Same oracle and tuning knowledge.
(4) OGM (d’Aspremont et al. 2021, Cor. 4.6) O(1+LR2/ε); stated on Rd. (1): Matches known order on Rd; no established improvement. (1): About 2 times more calls when LR2/ε≫1, on Rd.
(5) Classical GD (Drori and Teboulle 2012, Eq. (3.1)) O(1+LR2/ε); step 1/L, stated on Rd. (1): Known acceleration gives O(1+LR2/ε) instead of O(1+LR2/ε) on Rd. (2): Matches known rate; Lean formalization.
(6) Tight GD (Drori and Teboulle 2012, Thms. 3.1–3.2) O(1+LR2/ε); step 1/L, stated on Rd. (2): Matches known order on Rd; no established improvement. (2): About twice as many calls when LR2/ε≫1, for the same GD algorithm on Rd.
(7) FISTA (Beck and Teboulle 2009, Thm. 4.4) O(1+LR2/ε); constant step 1/L, g=0, E=Rd. (1): Matches known rate at g=0; no oracle saving, since the proximal map is the identity. (1): Up to one extra call at g=0. (1), (2): Do not cover the composite objectives also treated by (7).

Abbr: Costs count exact gradient evaluations. L: gradient Lipschitz constant; R: initial distance bound; ε: objective-gap tolerance; K: number of calls; d: dimension; GD: gradient descent; AGD: accelerated gradient descent; OGM: optimized gradient method; g: FISTA’s convex nonsmooth term.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Floor.Ring
import LongTails.Template

namespace LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  L : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ k seed x, HasGradientAt f (oracle.answer k (0, x) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed x y, ‖oracle.answer k (0, x) seed - oracle.answer k (0, y) seed‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex
